rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH -> warps wait on global loads: vectorize/widen loads, more elements per thread for loads in flight, prefetch earlier, fix coalescing / LOW -> memory latency is not the stall: stop adding ILP and restructure synchronization or launch geometry instead

proposal.blind_spot: The current metrics cannot tell whether these latency-bound kernels suffer from a grid that does not fill the GPU versus too many tiny blocks, nor whether their global loads are uncoalesced, so the optimizer cannot choose between exposing more parallelism, doing more work per block, or rewriting the data layout.

rationale.launch__waves_per_multiprocessor: HIGH -> keep grid saturated and give each program more work (process multiple rows/channels per program, larger BLOCK) / LOW -> split the reduction into more programs (two-stage/tree partials) to fill the SMs instead of serializing into fewer blocks
rationale.smsp__sass_average_data_bytes_per_sector: LOW -> fix uncoalesced loads: remap threads to consecutive addresses, avoid movedim/transpose materialization, load along the contiguous dim / HIGH -> leave layout alone and attack latency with more ILP and concurrent blocks rather than rewriting the access pattern

proposal.blind_spot: The optimizer cannot tell whether sub-peak DRAM utilization (78-87%) comes from too little launched or resident parallelism, which launch/occupancy changes would fix, or from a hard bandwidth ceiling where only reducing bytes helps.

rationale.launch__waves_per_multiprocessor: HIGH -> grid already fills the GPU, leave launch geometry alone and attack DRAM byte volume via fusion; LOW -> grid too small to saturate the bus, shrink BLOCK sizes or split the work across more programs to raise block count
rationale.sm__warps_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustain: LOW -> too few resident warps to hide memory latency, cut register/smem footprint per program or raise num_warps to lift occupancy; HIGH -> occupancy is fine, increase per-warp memory-level parallelism (vectorized loads, unrolling, num_stages) or treat DRAM as saturated and only reduce bytes

proposal.blind_spot: DRAM at 78-95% with idle compute cannot distinguish DRAM-bandwidth saturation from L2-bandwidth saturation from load-latency stalls, so the optimizer cannot choose between cutting DRAM bytes, keeping tiles in SMEM/registers, or adding memory-level parallelism.

rationale.lts__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustaine: HIGH -> L2 bandwidth is the real ceiling (likely where lts hit ~50%): fuse passes so intermediates stay in registers/shared memory instead of round-tripping through L2 / LOW -> L2 has headroom: keep reducing DRAM bytes and swizzle scheduling so unavoidable re-reads are served from L2
rationale.smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard: HIGH -> warps stall on global-load latency and DRAM is under-saturated: increase in-flight loads via 128-bit vectorization, more elements per thread, higher num_warps or num_stages pipelining / LOW -> latency is hidden and bandwidth is the true wall: only fewer bytes (fusion, removing materialized intermediates) will help, skip occupancy tuning

proposal.blind_spot: Current metrics show warps stalled on memory but cannot distinguish 'DRAM roof reached, only fewer bytes help' from 'memory pipeline underfed because occupancy/ILP is capped (possibly by registers)', which is exactly what separates the ~92%-DRAM kernels from the ~78%-DRAM ones.

rationale.smsp__warps_eligible.avg.per_cycle_activ: HIGH (>=1/cycle) -> DRAM is truly saturated, cut DRAM bytes via fusion/eliminating intermediates; LOW (~0) -> add memory-level parallelism: more num_warps, multiple independent loads per thread, prefetch/pipeline before consuming.
rationale.launch__occupancy_limit_registers: HIGH (registers bind below block/warp limit) -> shrink register footprint (smaller tile, recompute instead of caching, fewer unrolls) to raise occupancy and DRAM utilization; LOW -> occupancy cap is geometry/smem, change block size or launch shape instead of attacking registers.

split.chosen_by: llm_tiebreak:It splits kernels by normalized SM versus L2/LTS percent-of-peak throughput, which maps to real unit-saturation regimes and should generalize better than an absolute byte count or an arbitrary waves-per-SM cut.

proposal.blind_spot: The optimizer sees that DRAM is saturated but cannot tell whether the kernel's requested data volume is redundant (eliminable materialized operands, the winning pattern) or already at the logical minimum (nothing to remove, where rewrites only cause the observed regressions).

rationale.l1tex__t_sectors_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_: HIGH (requested load bytes >> logical input size) -> eliminate the redundant operand materialization, e.g. replace the expanded bias read with in-kernel broadcast indexing / LOW (requested ~= logical minimum) -> loads are compulsory, stop hunting for read-traffic reductions and keep the simple streaming access pattern

HIGH (requested store bytes >> logical output size) -> remove the extra intermediate write pass / materialized buffer copy / LOW (requested ~= output size) -> writes are minimal and DRAM is saturated, so the kernel is at the roofline: keep the original and avoid regressions like the 0.33x triu and 0.36x exp rewrites
